A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same R2M work. Their complete main text, figures, tables, equations, and appendices support reliable comparison despite added discussion and layout changes.

before.justification: v3 reports original dialogue and summarization evaluations, reward-model accuracy, ablations, computational measurements, and appendix hidden-state analyses.

after.justification: v4 retains these original empirical results, including Tables 1–5 and the experimental figures in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Algorithm 1 retain the same cross-attention aggregation, time-dependent weighting, GREBT objective, and lightweight reward-model updates. The new distributed-deployment suggestion preserves these computations.

E1.justification: UltraFeedback dialogue training, AlpacaEval 2 and MT-Bench evaluation, TL;DR summarization, and appendix analysis coverage are unchanged. The new multi-node discussion introduces no evaluated scenario.

E2.justification: Tables 1–2 retain SFT, ReMax, REINFORCE++, GRPO, RLOO, and the corresponding Pretrained RM, Iterative RMHead, and R2M w/o Train comparisons. Newly cited methods in Appendix B are not added to the experiments.

E3.justification: Section 5 and Appendix G retain the same models, metrics, sampling procedures, hyperparameters, and training budgets, including 51.2k dialogue and 1000k summarization trajectories. No experimental protocol accompanies the new discussion.

E4.justification: The Table 4 ablations, Figure 6 Gaussian-feedback replacement experiment, and Appendix C–D case and hidden-state analyses are unchanged. Section 6.2 adds theoretical discussion of reward noise, without new robustness measurements.

E5.justification: Experimental uncertainty reporting and run/seed information are unchanged. Section 6.2's Gaussian-noise assumption is theoretical; it introduces no empirical uncertainty estimates, confidence intervals, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All reported table entries and experimental graphics are retained. For example, LLaMA3 RLOO+R2M remains at 34.5% LC and 38.2% WR on AlpacaEval 2, and RLOO+R2M retains 81.6% WR on TL;DR.

T1.justification: New Section 6.2 adds an explicit uniform-softmax gradient derivation, Gaussian reward-noise assumptions, and an expected-gradient claim. The existing Theorems 3.1 and 4.1 and their Appendix A proofs remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same central claims: policy-hidden-state feedback enables lightweight, real-time reward-model alignment and mitigates reward overoptimization while improving downstream performance.

C2.justification: New Section 6 discusses distributed applicability and claims that GRE avoids artificial distinctions, preserves genuine quality differences, and suppresses noise-induced bias. These extend the mechanism and applicability explanations; the existing experimental interpretations remain intact.

D1.justification: Section 6.1 newly describes placing a cross-attention copy on the policy node, exchanging embeddings, estimating communication and module size, and synchronizing asynchronously. These are proposed deployment details; the documented experimental implementation remains unchanged.

R1.justification: Appendix B adds contextual citations on medical vision-language models, recommendation and graph adaptation, and reasoning and policy optimization, including PRPO and SpecExit. This broadens background coverage without substantially revising R2M's positioning against reward-overoptimization methods.

P1.justification: v4 inserts a Discussion section before the retained conclusion, expands the related-work paragraph, adds acknowledgements, and updates author/conference information and the impact heading. Most existing prose and the appendix organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: Figures 4 and 6 move between columns, with associated text, table, and appendix reflow. All nine figure graphics and five table structures are retained without redesign.

improvement.justification: Section 6.1 adds useful deployment ideas, but Section 6.2 introduces assurances of noise suppression and amplification of only genuine quality differences that its gradient calculation does not establish. Its identical-reward argument also leaves Equation 6's zero standard-deviation denominator unresolved, while Appendix A.9 assumes a positive standard deviation. With the method and empirical evidence unchanged, these added overstatements slightly weaken rigor.
